title: Existence of bilinear sheafification extension
statement: Let $(\mathcal C,J)$ be a site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], let $\mathcal O$ be a presheaf of commutative rings with sheafification $\mathcal O\to\mathcal O^\#$ [def-weil-pbc-sheafification], let $\mathcal F,\mathcal G$ be presheaves of $\mathcal O$-modules [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] with module sheafifications $\mathcal F\to\mathcal F^\#$, $\mathcal G\to\mathcal G^\#$, sheaves of $\mathcal O^\#$-modules [lem-pc-sites-module-sheafification-interface], and let $\mathcal H$ be a sheaf of $\mathcal O^\#$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], regarded as a presheaf of $\mathcal O$-modules by restriction of scalars. Every morphism of presheaves of sets $\beta:\mathcal F\times\mathcal G\to\mathcal H$ that is $\mathcal O$-bilinear on sections extends to a morphism of sheaves of sets $\beta^\#:\mathcal F^\#\times\mathcal G^\#\to\mathcal H$ that is $\mathcal O^\#$-bilinear and satisfies $\beta^\#\circ(\mathcal F\times\mathcal G\to\mathcal F^\#\times\mathcal G^\#)=\beta$.

source.place: Tag 0GMW, sheafification step in the construction of tensor products

proof.text: Use the Mathlib module sheafification units to obtain covering image sieves and covering equalizer sieves. For a pair of sheafified sections choose local lifts on the intersection of their image sieves. Local injectivity and separatedness of H make beta independent of lifts, and beta naturality proves compatibility.

Glue the compatible family using the sheaf condition of H. The amalgamation equation and lift independence yield its value on arbitrary lifts; separatedness on covering image sieves gives naturality, and the identity arrow gives the unit equation. This uses Presieve.IsSheafFor.amalgamate and valid_glue directly, rather than comparison of underlying set sheafifications.

On triple intersections of covering image sieves lift the sections needed for either additivity equation. For scalar equations also lift the scalar along alpha. Mathlib Sheafify.map_smul_eq identifies the scalar product of the lifted sections. Bilinearity of beta gives the local equations, separatedness of H descends them, and the four equations define the two curried linear maps.

theorem exists_bilinear_sheafification_extension
    {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C}
    [HasWeakSheafify J AddCommGrpCat.{max u v w}]
    [J.WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat.{max u v w}]
    (O : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ CommRingCat.{max u v w}) (R : Sheaf J CommRingCat.{max u v w})
    (α : (O ⋙ forget₂ CommRingCat.{max u v w} RingCat.{max u v w}) ⟶
      ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat.{max u v w} RingCat.{max u v w})).obj R).obj)
    [Presheaf.IsLocallyInjective J α] [Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective J α]
    (F G : PresheafOfModules.{max u v w} (O ⋙ forget₂ CommRingCat.{max u v w} RingCat.{max u v w}))
    (H : SheafOfModules.{max u v w}
      ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat.{max u v w} RingCat.{max u v w})).obj R))
    (β : ∀ X : Cᵒᵖ, F.obj X →ₗ[O.obj X] G.obj X →ₗ[O.obj X]
      ((restrictScalars α).obj H.val).obj X)
    (hβ : ∀ {X Y : Cᵒᵖ} (f : X ⟶ Y) (x : F.obj X) (y : G.obj X),
      β Y (F.map f x) (G.map f y) = H.val.map f (β X x y)) :
    ∃ γ : ∀ X : Cᵒᵖ,
      ((sheafification α).obj F).val.obj X →ₗ[R.obj.obj X]
        ((sheafification α).obj G).val.obj X →ₗ[R.obj.obj X] H.val.obj X,
      (∀ {X Y : Cᵒᵖ} (f : X ⟶ Y)
        (x : ((sheafification α).obj F).val.obj X)
        (y : ((sheafification α).obj G).val.obj X),
        γ Y (((sheafification α).obj F).val.map f x)
          (((sheafification α).obj G).val.map f y) = H.val.map f (γ X x y)) ∧
      (∀ (X : Cᵒᵖ) (x : F.obj X) (y : G.obj X),
        γ X (((sheafificationAdjunction α).unit.app F).app X x)
          (((sheafificationAdjunction α).unit.app G).app X y) = β X x y)
